question: Can the publicly reusable MakiBIS checklist registered by the ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity supply fish-species evidence for the Makiling waters?

sourceMetadata.title: Makiling Biodiversity Information System (MAKIBIS)
sourceMetadata.license: CC0 1.0; the ACB IPT rights statement says the publisher waived rights to the data and dedicated it to the public domain.

gbifTaxonApiScreen.interpretation: The 275 API name usages comprise 250 genus usages plus 25 higher-rank classification usages; all returned usages are in plant groups. The IPT archive's 250 core records and the API's 275 indexed usages are different counts and are not conflated. No species-rank or chordate/fish name usage is indexed in this dataset.

obisOccurrenceCheck.interpretation: This OBIS dataset page reports zero occurrence records. The related GBIF registration is a taxonomic checklist, not an occurrence feed. Neither can support fish presence or absence claims for Makiling waters.

decision.reason: The current openly licensed GBIF checklist is plant-rank-only and has no species-rank taxa; its OBIS counterpart reports no occurrence records. MakiBIS's broader portal description is not evidence that this particular registered checklist contains fish.

limitations: The dataset's CC0 license supports reuse of this published checklist, but does not supply fish evidence where none is present.
The broader MakiBIS portal may contain fish information elsewhere; this review covers only the specified ACB GBIF/OBIS resources and does not claim the portal has no fish data.
No present-day fish presence, absence, abundance, water quality, safety, catchability, fishing access, legal rule, diet, bait recommendation, photo, or geometry is established.
nextAction: Continue searching independently reusable fish checklists and locality-resolved fish surveys; keep MakiBIS as a plant-only source for this GBIF registration unless a distinct fish dataset is identified.
